title: Strings
summary: Linear-time pattern matching by letting a string describe its own structure.

articles.title: Prefix function and KMP
articles.summary: For every prefix, the longest border that is both a proper prefix and a suffix — the engine behind linear-time matching.
articles.idea_md:
A **border** of a string is a proper prefix that is also a suffix: `ab` is a border of `abcab`. The prefix function records, for every position `i`, the length of the longest border of `s[0..i]`:

| `i` | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `s[i]` | a | b | a | c | a | b | a | b |
| `π[i]` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 2 |

Computing it naively compares every prefix with every suffix. The linear algorithm reuses what it already knows. To get `π[i]`, try to extend the previous border `k = π[i−1]`: if `s[i] == s[k]`, the answer is `k + 1`. If not, the next candidate is not `k − 1` but the **border of that border**, `π[k−1]` — the longest shorter string that is still both a prefix and a suffix. Keep falling back until the characters match or `k` reaches `0`.

Each step of `i` raises `k` by at most one, and every fallback lowers it, so the total work is `O(n)`.

**Pattern matching (Knuth–Morris–Pratt).** Compute the prefix function of `pattern + sep + text`, where `sep` occurs in neither string. Wherever `π` equals the pattern's length, a full copy of the pattern ends there. Finding every occurrence costs `O(|pattern| + |text|)`, with no backtracking in the text.
articles.formula: \pi[i] = \max \left\{ k \le i : s_{0 \ldots k-1} = s_{i-k+1 \ldots i} \right\}
articles.applications_md:
- **Exact pattern matching** in linear time, including streaming text where you cannot look back.
- **Periods and repetitions**: the shortest period of a string is `n − π[n−1]` when it divides `n`.
- **Counting prefix occurrences**, building a string-matching automaton, and the shortest palindrome made by adding characters in front of `s` (the longest palindromic prefix is the last value of the prefix function of `s + sep + reverse(s)`).
articles.pitfall_md:
- The separator must not occur in the pattern or the text; otherwise a match can straddle it.
- Falling back with `k = k − 1` instead of `k = π[k−1]` is wrong, not just slow: on `ababb` it reports `π[4] = 2`, although `ab` is not a suffix of `ababb` (the right answer is `0`).
- `π[i]` is the length of a **proper** border: `π[0]` is always `0`, never `1`.

articles.title: Z-function
articles.summary: For every position, how long the string starting there agrees with the string’s own beginning.
articles.idea_md:
`z[i]` is the length of the longest common prefix of `s` and the suffix that starts at `i`. For `s = aabcaabxaaz`, `z[4] = 3` because `aab` starts both the string and position `4`, and the next characters (`c` and `x`) differ. By convention `z[0]` is left `0`.

Comparing every suffix with the whole string would be quadratic. The linear algorithm remembers the **Z-box**: the window `[l, r)` that reaches furthest right among the matches found so far. Everything inside it is a copy of `s[0 .. r−l)`.

For a new position `i`:

- If `i` lies inside the box, the character run at `i` mirrors the one at `i − l`, so `z[i]` is at least `min(r − i, z[i − l])` — no comparisons needed for that part.
- Then extend by comparing characters directly, and if the match now reaches beyond `r`, move the box to `[i, i + z[i])`.

Every successful direct comparison pushes `r` to the right, and `r` never moves left, so the whole array costs `O(n)`.

For **pattern matching**, compute the Z-function of `pattern + sep + text`: a position in the text part whose value is at least `|pattern|` starts an occurrence.
articles.formula: z[i] = \max \left\{ k : s_{0 \ldots k-1} = s_{i \ldots i+k-1} \right\}
articles.applications_md:
- **Pattern matching** in `O(|pattern| + |text|)`, an alternative to KMP that many find easier to reason about.
- **Counting distinct substrings** incrementally, or finding the shortest period (the first `i` with `i + z[i] = n` and `n` divisible by `i`).
- **String compression and repetition checks**, and comparing a string with its own shifts.
articles.pitfall_md:
- The copy step must take `min(r − i, z[i − l])`: copying `z[i − l]` alone can run past the window, where nothing is known.
- Forgetting to move the window after a longer match keeps the algorithm correct but quadratic.
- As with KMP, the separator in `pattern + sep + text` must not appear in either string.
